answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. The protection comes from the fact that every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer, so flooding the jury floods the attacker with its own cost. This is why the network can stay open without a central gatekeeper: the economics of reputation do the filtering that a trusted authority otherwise would. Consider a voyage as the anchor of the cost. A nadir stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a velvet hold...
